Analyze your first NIS cohort

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

Use invented discharges to build a cohort, make a Table 1, and fit a survey-weighted model.

library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
library(gtsummary)

Open the files and define the analysis groups 

files <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
nis <- nis_open(files, years = 2019:2020) |>
  select(nis_vars_design(), nis_vars_dx(), AGE, LOS, DIED, DISPUNIFORM) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50") |>
  nis_outcomes()

files is a directory of annual Parquet files. The query keeps the design fields and analysis columns. The flag checks every diagnosis slot for I50.

Estimate discharge totals and length of stay 

design <- nis_design(
  nis, cohort = AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, heart_failure, los_days, in_hospital_death)
)

estimates <- design |>
  group_by(heart_failure) |>
  summarise(discharges = survey_total(), mean_los = survey_mean(los_days))
estimates
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   heart_failure discharges discharges_se mean_los mean_los_se
#>   <lgl>              <dbl>         <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 FALSE               104           19.9     5.38       0.273
#> 2 TRUE                125.          17.3     5.66       0.229

You get a weighted discharge total and mean length of stay for each heart-failure group, with standard errors. Pass eligibility to cohort so hospitals without adult discharges still count in the sampling structure. The totals cover both years. How easyNIS works

Make a table and fit a model 

design |>
  mutate(heart_failure = factor(
    heart_failure,
    levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
    labels = c("No heart failure", "Heart failure")
  )) |>
  tbl_svysummary(
    by = heart_failure,
    include = c(AGE, los_days, in_hospital_death),
    label = list(
      AGE ~ "Age (years)",
      los_days ~ "Length of stay (days)",
      in_hospital_death ~ "In-hospital death"
    )
  ) |>
  nis_suppress() |>
  as_gt()
Characteristic No heart failure
N = 1041,2 		Heart failure
N = 1251,2
Age (years) 65 (49, 77) 59 (41, 76)
Length of stay (days) 5.0 (2.0, 8.0) 6.0 (3.0, 9.0)
In-hospital death ≤10 ≤10
1 Median (Q1, Q3); n (%)
2 Statistics based on unweighted n ≤10 are marked ≤10; cells contributed by fewer than two distinct year-scoped hospitals are marked '<2 hospitals', regardless of count. The discharge-count mask takes precedence when both rules apply. Dichotomous rows with a protected complement are marked 'Masked' when the displayed event passes both rules. When a categorical variable has one masked level in a column, the smallest remaining positive level is marked 'Masked'. Before sharing under the HCUP Data Use Agreement, review tables for other derivable cells.

The table compares the groups and masks cells with too few sampled discharges or contributing hospitals.

fit <- survey::svyglm(
  in_hospital_death ~ heart_failure + AGE,
  design = design, family = quasibinomial()
)
tbl_regression(
  fit,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  label = list(heart_failure ~ "Heart failure", AGE ~ "Age (years)")
) |>
  as_gt()
Characteristic OR 95% CI p-value
Heart failure


    FALSE — —
    TRUE 0.53 0.04, 7.00 0.6
Age (years) 0.91 0.89, 0.94 <0.001
Abbreviations: CI = Confidence Interval, OR = Odds Ratio

The heart failure odds ratio compares the odds of in-hospital death between the two groups, adjusting for age. Before sharing a model fitted to real data, review the discharges that contributed to the fit for disclosure risk.

Check the design and export a summary 

nis_design_report(design)
#> NIS design report
#> Years: 2019, 2020
#> Weights: DISCWT
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   stage           discharges
#>   <chr>                <dbl>
#> 1 Input sample           192
#> 2 Original cohort        192
#> 3 Current domain         192

reviewed <- estimates |>
  left_join(nis_cell_counts(design, by = heart_failure), by = "heart_failure") |>
  nis_suppress(
    count_col = n, hospital_col = hospitals,
    weighted_cols = c(discharges, discharges_se, mean_los, mean_los_se)
  )
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(reviewed, file, row.names = FALSE)
read.csv(file)
#>   heart_failure discharges discharges_se mean_los mean_los_se   n hospitals
#> 1         FALSE      104.0      19.90779 5.380769   0.2727846  84        24
#> 2          TRUE      124.8      17.34820 5.663462   0.2289912 108        18

The design report records which years and weights entered the analysis and how many sampled discharges met the criteria. Check support for each statistic before export. For example, a mean with missing values needs counts restricted to the records used for that mean. Review the release across all outputs. Check disclosure
